title: Unit and coefficient associativity of compact-support projection maps
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$ of its valuation ring, and $n\geq1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes, let $f:X\to Y$ be separated and of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and fix a compactification $c=(j,r)$ with $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{r}Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Work in the ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], with derived tensor [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Put $P=Rf_!^c=Rr_*j_!$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] and $S=Lf^*$ [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], with its canonical strong monoidal structure [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso, def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. Let $\delta_{B,B'}:S(B\otimes B')\xrightarrow{\sim}SB\otimes SB'$ and $e:S\mathbf1_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf1_X$ be its inverse structure maps. Here $\mathbf1_T=A_T$ in degree zero, and $\otimes$ denotes the derived tensor.
For $M\in D^b_c(X,A)$ and $B\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], use exactly the compactification projection transformation $\operatorname{PF}^c_{M,B}:PM\otimes B\to P(M\otimes SB)$ of [def-exchange-projection]. Where these maps are invertible, define
$$\pi_{B,M}:P(SB\otimes M)\xrightarrow{P(\beta_{SB,M})}P(M\otimes SB)\xrightarrow{(\operatorname{PF}^c_{M,B})^{-1}}PM\otimes B\xrightarrow{\beta_{PM,B}}B\otimes PM,$$
where $\beta$ is tensor symmetry. Invertibility is a separate hypothesis here, not part of the conclusion.
These inverse projection maps satisfy the unit and coefficient-variable associativity equations of [def-sfb-projection-formula]. Explicitly, for $B,B'\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ and $M\in D^b_c(X,A)$, whenever all projection components in the following expressions are invertible,
$$\lambda_{PM}\circ\pi_{\mathbf1_Y,M}=P\bigl(\lambda_M\circ(e\otimes1_M)\bigr),$$
$$\alpha_{B,B',PM}\circ\pi_{B\otimes B',M}
=(1_B\otimes\pi_{B',M})\circ\pi_{B,SB'\otimes M}\circ P\bigl(\alpha_{SB,SB',M}\circ(\delta_{B,B'}\otimes1_M)\bigr).$$
Here $\alpha$ and $\lambda$ are the canonical derived tensor associator and left unitor, and all equations are equalities of derived morphisms at the fixed compactification. All displayed tensor inputs belong to the stated constructible domains; one coefficient factor of finite Tor amplitude suffices for each product with $M$. No right adjoint to $P$, smoothness, purity, or compatibility with composition of two geometric morphisms is assumed or concluded.

proof.text: In the ambient derived categories put $F=Lr^*$, $R=Rr_*$, $Q=Lj^*$, $J=j_!$, $P=RJ$, $S=QF$. The canonical symmetric monoidal comparisons satisfy $\delta^S=\delta^Q Q\delta^F$ and $e_S=e_Q Qe_F$ [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso, lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Apply [lem-pur-adjoint-left-projection-action] to $F\dashv R$ and its specified counit projection $\rho$, obtaining $t$ and both forward laws. Apply [lem-pur-open-left-projection-action] to the open unit and normalized $\gamma$ of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], obtaining $v$ and both forward laws. Neither application requires a projection inverse.

source.place: Tags 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), 0GL1 (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor); fixed compactification, coefficient constraints supporting blueprint (G13)

proof.text: Define $T_{B,M}=P(\beta_{M,SB})\operatorname{PF}^c_{M,B}\beta_{B,PM}$. Substitution of the exact composite in [def-exchange-projection] cancels the adjacent symmetries at $FB,JM$, giving $T_{B,M}=R(v_{FB,M})t_{B,JM}$. Apply [lem-pur-composite-left-projection-action] to obtain $P(h^S_M)T_{\mathbf1,M}=\lambda_{PM}$ and $P(a^S_{B,B',M})T_{B\otimes B',M}=T_{B,SB'\otimes M}(1_B\otimes T_{B',M})\alpha_{B,B',PM}$, where $h^S_M=\lambda_M(e_S\otimes1)$ and $a^S=\alpha(\delta^S\otimes1)$.

proof.text: For exactly the assumed invertible components, symmetry squared is identity, hence $T_{B,M}^{-1}=\beta_{PM,B}(\operatorname{PF}^c_{M,B})^{-1}P(\beta_{SB,M})=\pi_{B,M}$. Right-compose the unit law with $\pi_{\mathbf1,M}$. Right-compose the coefficient law with $\pi_{B\otimes B',M}$, then left-compose with $\pi_{B,SB'\otimes M}$ and $1_B\otimes\pi_{B',M}$. Cancellation gives precisely the two displayed equations, with the constraints of [def-sfb-projection-formula].

proof.text: [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] makes $SB,SB',S(B\otimes B')$ finite Tor. [lem-sf-tensor-ctf](ii) makes $B\otimes B'$ and $SB\otimes SB'$ finite Tor; (i) makes every tensor with $M$ bounded constructible, regardless of Tor amplitude of $M$. [prop-finite-compact-support-constructibility] makes their $P$-images bounded constructible at the chosen compactification, and (i) again handles all coefficient tensors with those images. These lemmas require finite-type schemes over $k$ and separated finite-type $f$, not absolute separatedness. The unit $A_T[0]$ is constructible and flat with Tor interval $[0,0]$: tensoring with it is the identity. Thus every displayed input lies in its stated domain, including empty schemes, zero objects and unit coefficients.

(1) lem-pur-adjoint-left-projection-action (base Steps 2-proper, 3, 4) is true. Here ρ is the adjunct of (ε⊗1)δ, which is exactly π_p in def-exchange-projection and Stacks 0B56. The transpose (1⊗ε)δ follows from counit naturality, F symmetric and β²=1. The unit law follows from the unit axiom of def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor. Associativity follows from (1) used twice plus the associativity axiom. No invertibility is used. (2) lem-pur-open-left-projection-action (base Steps 2-open, 5) is true. On Hom(JX,Y), f↦Q(f)u is the adjunction bijection, so Q is injective on maps out of objects isomorphic to ones in im J. Both sources qualify, through λ and through v (an isomorphism). I wrote out both reductions, via the normalization and Q's monoidal axioms. Its hypotheses match the statement of lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization: invertible unit, fully faithful j_!, and j^*γ equal to the identity after the unit and μ_j; for constant A its γ is the map that def-exchange-projection uses. (3) lem-pur-composite-left-projection-action (base Steps 6, 7) is true. It uses naturality of t at v, the t-law, the v-law at (FB,FB'), naturality of v at δ^F, and a^Q(Qδ^F⊗1)=a^S; the unit case is the same with e_F. Assembly Step 2: T = R(v)t after one cancellation of a β-pair, written out against the PF^c composite. Step 3's inversion order matches def-sfb-projection-formula. Step 4's hypotheses were checked against lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude, lem-sf-tensor-ctf (i)/(ii) and prop-finite-compact-support-constructibility, and M never needs finite Tor. Possible duplicates checked: lem-pur-finite-projection-action-laws is the geometric right-coefficient identity in another unit and has no unit law or detection argument. lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-associativity, lem-sfb-ringed-projection-canonical-normalization, lem-sfb-monoidal-adjunction-unit-counit, lem-amb-compactification-projection-composition and lem-asd-adjunction-projection-map-mate state other things.
